findings.description: Stripping leading dots from each no_proxy entry and then prefixing a single dot changes matching for entries that were not dot-prefixed, and an empty or '.'-only entry becomes a match-all.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a no_proxy list that contains an empty string, such as 'localhost,' or 'a.com,,b.com', or a bare '.'. After lstrip the entry is '', so hostname == host is false, but host becomes '.', and any hostname containing a dot (for example 'example.com') ends with '.' only if it ends with a dot, so the match is unlikely. Before the change, an empty host made endswith('') true, so the behavior was already match-all. The remaining difference is that an entry like 'example.com' now only matches 'example.com' or '.example.com' suffixes, whereas the old code also matched 'badexample.com'. That is arguably a fix, but 'host_with_port' entries such as 'example.com:8080' are handled differently because the dot is prepended. Impact: low risk of changed proxy-bypass behavior.
